title: Domain Concierge: anchor-driven sampling pipeline for per-domain calibration bundles
creator: Isabela Cruz
description: Goal: build a reproducible, auditable pipeline that produces small, per-domain calibration bundles ("packs") optimized for FP8 and INT8 quantization validation. These packs should preserve rare but high-impact prompt patterns, represent temporal recency, reflect production context-length distributions, and include anchor exemplars that stabilize quantization drift across model variants. The pipeline must integrate with the existing eval harness, produce deterministic seeds for re-runs, and surface dataset metadata to Console for inspection. This ticket implements the sampling/curation component and the first validation sweep against a subset of production tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline can generate a calibration pack for a domain in <= 30 minutes for 1M input corpus
Each pack contains: anchor set (100–500 exemplars), stratified buckets for token-length and context-length, and a diversity subset; total pack sizes configurable between 1K–50K examples
Calibration packs yield <= 1.5% degradation in generation NLL vs gold validation for FP8 prototype across sampled domains (target adjustable per domain)
All packs include provenance metadata (tenant-id hashed, sampling seed, time window, sampling weights) and are exportable to S3 with lifecycle tags
Integration test: eval-harness job passes end-to-end (pack -> quantize -> validate) and uploads metrics dashboard to /redwood/quant/pack-results
design_notes: We avoid naive frequency sampling — it overfits to common templated prompts and misses long-tail failure modes.
Anchor-driven approach: compute domain fingerprints (shingled n-gram hashes + embedding clusters) and select stable exemplars per fingerprint to act as anchors across packs.
Recency weighting: apply a decay function w(t)=exp(-alpha * age_days) with configurable alpha per domain; alpha defaults to 0.03 for consumer-facing domains, 0.005 for legacy enterprise workloads.
Context buckets: preserve distribution of context lengths (0–128, 129–512, 513–2048, >2048 tokens) to reflect KV cache states encountered in production.
We will surface trade-offs in Console: pack size vs calibration variance, anchor size vs coverage, and oversample factor for rare cohorts.
sampling_algorithm: Step 1: Ingest de-identified production prompts for a domain and compute lightweight fingerprint (context-length, response-length, shingle-signature, coarse intent label).
Step 2: Run reservoir sampling per fingerprint with priority weight = base_freq^{-0.5} * recency_weight * novelty_boost.
Step 3: Anchor selection: from top-k fingerprints by risk-score pick canonical exemplars using embedding-distance medoids to ensure representativeness.
Step 4: Diversity pass: compute token-level entropy and add top N high-entropy examples to capture failure cases.
Step 5: Soft-prune similar examples using locality-sensitive hashing to keep near-duplicates under 3% of pack.
Step 6: Output pack with deterministic seed, per-example provenance, and recommended quantization slices (int8/FP8 target columns).
calibration_pack_spec: Default pack size: 5,000 examples for mid-sized domains; configurable [1k, 50k].
Anchor set: 250 exemplars (tunable 100–500). Anchors always included in final pack and flagged in metadata.
Buckets: token-length (quartiles), context-length (explicit ranges), response-shape (short/medium/long), and traffic-cohort (web/api/batch).
Oversampling policy: rare-cohort multiplier up to x10 with cap at 15% of total pack to avoid calibration bias.
Metadata: sampling_seed, created_by, domain_hash, time_window_start/end, sampling_config_ref (S3 path).
validation_plan: Run end-to-end quantization validation using eval-harness (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness, branch=pack-integration) for both FP8 and INT8 profiles.
Metrics: per-example NLL delta, token-level KL divergence against fp32 baseline, sample-level hallucination rate, and latency impact for runtime-1.20 kernels.
Stability test: re-sample with 5 different seeds and measure variance in metrics; target standard deviation < 0.75% for primary metrics.
A/B test: compare packs generated with and without anchor exemplars on a holdout domain to quantify anchor utility.
Upload results to Console dashboard and create alert if any domain shows >2% degradation on regression metrics.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: PoC reservoir+anchor pipeline implemented in prototype notebook; ran on 2 domains (support-chat, marketplace-search). Initial packs look diverse and anchors surface high-risk prompts.

2026-03-04: Engineering review with Luca Moretti and Jun Park. Decided to persist fingerprints in Dynamo for incremental updates rather than full re-index per run. Action: ENG infra ticket to add TTL-indexed table.

2026-03-06: First integration with eval-harness completed; FP8 prototype showed 1.9% mean delta on NLL for marketplace-search — above target. Hypothesis: token-length distribution mismatch; we will increase long-context bucket representation.

2026-03-09: Trade-off discussion: raising rare-cohort oversample reduces average NLL but increases variance on common prompts. Agreed to cap oversampling at 15% and add a 'calibration-stability' metric in outputs.

2026-03-12: Ran deterministic re-samples (5 seeds) for support-chat domain; stdev 0.62% on NLL and anchor exemplars improved worst-case tail by ~12%. Preparing PR for pipeline code and evaluation graphs.
links: Infra task: ENG-431256 (add TTL fingerprint table)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting packs to recent spikes (e.g., a bot attack) — Mitigation: apply anomaly filter and require min-unique-authors threshold before raising recency weight.
Risk: PII leakage through prompts — Mitigation: enforce de-identification step (token redaction) before sampling and record hash of original prompt only.
Risk: Increased variance for downstream customers after quant rollout — Mitigation: per-domain rollout gating and automated rollback using Canary metrics in Console.
